```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Pan_2019_rituximab")()$meta$reference`
* Description: `r readModelDb("Pan_2019_rituximab")()$meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.13970> (open access, PMC6624401)

Rituximab concentrations were not measured in this retrospective cohort, so
Pan 2019 fitted a kinetic-pharmacodynamic (K-PD) model: each dose (in mg) is
added to a virtual compartment that decays first-order, and the residual dose
drives a saturable increase in the loss rate of a CD19+ lymphocyte turnover
pool. Pan 2019 Eqs 1-2 and the `$DES` block of the NONMEM file in the
supplementary material:

```
dA1/dt = -KE * A1
DG     = EMAX * A1 / (ED50 + A1)
dA2/dt = KIN - KOUT * (1 + DG) * A2,   A2(0) = BSL,  KIN = BSL * KOUT
EMAX   = THETA_EMAX * (1 + 0.381 * CTX) * (1 + 0.657 * MTX)
```

In the packaged model `A1` is `depot_kpd` (mg) and `A2` is `bcell`
(CD19+ count, 10^6/L), which is also the observed output.

# Population

Thirty-nine children treated with rituximab for autoimmune disease at Great
Ormond Street Hospital, London, between 2010 and 2016 contributed 258 CD19+
lymphocyte counts (Pan 2019 Table 1). Median age was 13.2 years (range
3.9-18); 34 of 39 were female. Twenty-two had systemic lupus erythematosus;
the others had granulomatosis with polyangiitis (6), juvenile dermatomyositis
(4), anti-SRP positive myositis (3), and one each of juvenile idiopathic
arthritis, lupus overlap syndrome, ANCA-positive vasculitis and polyarteritis
nodosa. Rituximab was given as 2 x 750 mg/m^2 (days 1 and 15) or
4 x 375 mg/m^2 (days 1, 8, 15 and 22); the per-infusion dose had a median of
1000 mg (range 413-1000). All children received prednisolone and
methylprednisolone; 25.6% received methotrexate and 43.6% cyclophosphamide.
The median baseline CD19+ count was 170 x 10^6/L (range 10-940). 108 counts
reported as zero were set to 5 x 10^6/L (half the lowest detectable count).

The same information is in the model's `population` metadata.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Virtual-dose ODE `d/dt(depot_kpd) = -kel * depot_kpd` | | Eq 1; supplement `$DES` |
| B-cell ODE with `1 + Emax * A1 / (ED50 + A1)` on the loss rate | | Eq 2; supplement `$DES` |
| `kin = rbase * kout`, `bcell(0) = rbase` | | Methods; supplement `$PK` (`KIN = BSL * KOUT`, `A_0(2) = BSL`) |
| Comedication effects multiply Emax | | supplement `$PK` (`EMAX = THETA(4) * (1 + CCOV) * (1 + CCOV1)`) |
| `lkel` | log(0.0359064) 1/day | supplement `$THETA(1)`; Table 2 ke 0.036 |
| `lrbase` | log(266.449) 10^6/L | supplement `$THETA(2)`; Table 2 Baseline 266.4 |
| `lkout` | log(0.0160064) 1/day | supplement `$THETA(3)`; Table 2 kout 0.02 |
| `lemax` | log(35.1538) | supplement `$THETA(4)`; Table 2 Emax 35.2 |
| `led50` | log(0.811751) mg | supplement `$THETA(5)`; Table 2 ED50 0.81 |
| `e_conmed_cyclophosphamide_emax` | 0.381171 | supplement `$THETA(7)`; Table 2 covCYC 0.38 |
| `e_conmed_mtx_emax` | 0.657277 | supplement `$THETA(8)`; Table 2 covMTX 0.66 |
| `etalkel` | 0.54598 | supplement `$OMEGA`; Table 2 BSV 73.88% = 100 * sqrt(0.54598) |
| `etalrbase` | 0.96308 | supplement `$OMEGA`; Table 2 BSV 98.13% |
| `etalkout` | 0.803053 | supplement `$OMEGA`; Table 2 BSV 89.61% |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.351255) = 0.5927 | supplement `$THETA(6)` (a variance, see below); Table 2 59.3% |
| `addSd` | fixed(0.01) 10^6/L | supplement `$ERROR`: `SD = SQRT(0.0001 + CV * IPRED**2)` |

The supplement `$ERROR` block is `SD = SQRT(0.0001 + CV * IPRED**2)` with
`$SIGMA 1 FIX`, so `THETA(6)` is the proportional variance and 0.0001 a fixed
additive variance. Table 2 confirms this: its 59.3% is `sqrt(0.351255)`. The
packaged model writes this as `add(addSd) + prop(propSd) + combined2()`.

# Simulation set-up

Doses are prescribed in mg/m^2 but the model takes mg. Pan 2019 does not give
the body-surface area used for its simulations; this vignette uses 1.33 m^2,
for which 750 mg/m^2 equals the cohort's median per-infusion dose of 1000 mg
(Table 1). The four regimens are those of Pan 2019 Figure 4 and Table 3.

```{r setup-sim}
mod <- readModelDb("Pan_2019_rituximab")
bsa <- 1.33
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,                   ~dose_mg_m2,
  "750 mg/m2: 2 infusions",   750,
  "375 mg/m2: 4 infusions",   375,
  "750 mg/m2: 1 infusion",    750,
  "375 mg/m2: 1 infusion",    375
)
dose_days <- list(
  "750 mg/m2: 2 infusions" = c(0, 14),
  "375 mg/m2: 4 infusions" = c(0, 7, 14, 21),
  "750 mg/m2: 1 infusion" = 0,
  "375 mg/m2: 1 infusion" = 0
)

make_events <- function(reg, ids, obs_times) {
  row <- regimens[regimens$regimen == reg, ]
  doses <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = dose_days[[reg]]) |>
    mutate(amt = row$dose_mg_m2 * bsa, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot_kpd")
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "bcell")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(regimen = reg, CONMED_MTX = 0L, CONMED_CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE = 0L)
}
```

# Typical-value profiles (Figure 4, right panel)

```{r typical}
typ <- bind_rows(lapply(regimens$regimen, function(reg) {
  ev <- make_events(reg, 1L, seq(0, 364, by = 0.5))
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  s$regimen <- reg
  s
}))
typ$regimen <- factor(typ$regimen, levels = regimens$regimen)

ggplot(typ, aes(time / 7, bcell, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("purple", "darkgreen", "blue", "red")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "CD19+ lymphocyte count (10^6/L)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 (right panel) of Pan 2019: typical patient, no comedication."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The four curves fall to the same nadir and separate during recovery, lower
doses recovering first, as in the published panel. The digitised values below
were read from that panel by the maintainers (log axis calibrated on its 10
and 100 gridlines; the green curve overlaps the others before week 40).

```{r fig4-compare}
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,                  ~week, ~published,
  "750 mg/m2: 2 infusions",  20,    7.8,
  "750 mg/m2: 2 infusions",  30,    12.3,
  "750 mg/m2: 2 infusions",  40,    47.1,
  "750 mg/m2: 2 infusions",  50,    139.6,
  "375 mg/m2: 4 infusions",  40,    37.9,
  "375 mg/m2: 4 infusions",  50,    125.7,
  "750 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   20,    8.4,
  "750 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   30,    19.5,
  "750 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   40,    78.2,
  "750 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   50,    174,
  "375 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   20,    9.5,
  "375 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   30,    29.1,
  "375 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   40,    104.8,
  "375 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   50,    194
)
fig4_cmp <- fig4 |>
  left_join(
    typ |> filter(time %in% (7 * c(20, 30, 40, 50))) |>
      transmute(regimen = as.character(regimen), week = time / 7, simulated = bcell),
    by = c("regimen", "week")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated - published) / published)
stopifnot(nrow(fig4_cmp) == nrow(fig4), !anyNA(fig4_cmp$simulated))
fig4_cmp |>
  mutate(simulated = signif(simulated, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    Regimen = regimen, Week = week, "Figure 4 (digitised)" = published,
    Simulated = simulated, "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r fig4-assert}
# Deterministic typical-value solve against values digitised from a 2-pixel
# line on a log axis (1 pixel is ~1% of the value). The BSA used by the authors
# is unknown and shifts the recovery limb of each curve, so the bound allows
# for that; a wrong kel, kout or Emax moves the week-40 values by far more.
stopifnot(
  median(abs(fig4_cmp$pct_diff)) < 15,
  max(abs(fig4_cmp$pct_diff)) < 35
)
```

The simulated curves sit 2-16% below the digitised ones on the recovery limb,
that is, the published curves recover slightly sooner. The BSA is the obvious
unreported input: the same comparison with 1.0 m^2 in place of 1.33 m^2 gives
a median absolute difference of 0.5% (largest 15.6%), while simulating with
the rounded Table 2 `kout` of 0.02 per day instead of the fitted 0.0160 gives
4.2% (largest 14.6%). Either could explain the gap, so neither the BSA
assumption nor any parameter is changed to close it.

## Deterministic checks

* While the drug effect is saturated the count settles at
  `rbase / (1 + Emax)` = 266.449 / 36.1538 = 7.37 x 10^6/L, the flat
  nadir of every curve in Figure 4.
* Doubling a single dose keeps the virtual dose above any level for an extra
  `log(2) / kel` = 19.3 days, so the 750 mg/m^2 single-infusion curve should
  recover to 100 x 10^6/L about 19.3 days after the 375 mg/m^2 curve.
* Without rituximab the count stays at its baseline.

```{r deterministic}
nadir <- typ |> group_by(regimen) |> summarise(nadir = min(bcell))
nadir_expected <- 266.449 / (1 + 35.1538)
stopifnot(all(abs(nadir$nadir / nadir_expected - 1) < 0.01))

t_recover <- function(reg, level = 100) {
  d <- typ[typ$regimen == reg & typ$time > 28, ]
  d$time[which(d$bcell >= level)[1]]
}
shift_days <- t_recover("750 mg/m2: 1 infusion") - t_recover("375 mg/m2: 1 infusion")
stopifnot(abs(shift_days - log(2) / 0.0359064) < 1.5)

nodose <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 365, by = 5), cmt = "bcell"),
  params = c(CONMED_MTX = 0, CONMED_CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE = 0),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
stopifnot(max(abs(nodose$bcell - 266.449)) < 1e-6 * 266.449)

data.frame(
  check = c("Nadir (10^6/L)", "Recovery shift 750 vs 375 mg/m2 single (days)"),
  expected = c(nadir_expected, log(2) / 0.0359064),
  simulated = c(mean(nadir$nadir), shift_days)
) |>
  mutate(across(c(expected, simulated), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  rename(Check = check, Expected = expected, Simulated = simulated) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Pan 2019 also reports 6.2% and 3.3% of baseline remaining after 6 months for
the single and the four-infusion 375 mg/m^2 regimens:

```{r six-month}
typ |>
  filter(time == 182, regimen %in% c("375 mg/m2: 1 infusion", "375 mg/m2: 4 infusions")) |>
  transmute(
    Regimen = regimen,
    "Simulated % of baseline at 26 weeks" = round(100 * bcell / 266.449, 1),
    "Pan 2019 Results" = c(3.3, 6.2)[match(regimen, c("375 mg/m2: 4 infusions", "375 mg/m2: 1 infusion"))]
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The four-infusion value matches. The single-infusion value is on the steep
recovery limb, where it depends on the dose in mg and therefore on the BSA
assumed above.

# Virtual dose: PKNCA

There is no measured rituximab exposure in Pan 2019, but the K-PD virtual
dose has a half-life that the paper reports (19 days, Results; median 19.3,
Discussion). PKNCA is run on the typical-value virtual-dose amount after a
single 750 mg/m^2 infusion.

```{r pknca}
vd <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  make_events("750 mg/m2: 1 infusion", 1L, c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, seq(7, 182, by = 7))),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "750 mg/m2 single infusion") |>
  filter(!is.na(depot_kpd))
dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 750 * bsa, treatment = "750 mg/m2 single infusion")
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(vd, depot_kpd ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = data.frame(treatment = "750 mg/m2 single infusion", half.life = 19.3),
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "day"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Virtual-dose half-life against the Pan 2019 value.")
hl <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |> filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |> pull(PPORRES)
stopifnot(length(hl) == 1L, abs(hl / 19.3 - 1) < 0.02)
```

# Suppression time (Table 3)

Pan 2019 Table 3 gives the median (95% prediction interval) time spent below
10 and below 100 x 10^6/L "for patients starting with normal CD19+ counts"
(above 200 x 10^6/L). Every lower 95% bound in Table 3 is above zero, so in
the published simulation every patient went below 10 x 10^6/L. With the
baseline drawn from its full between-subject distribution that is impossible:
a patient without comedication bottoms out at `baseline / 36.2`, which stays
above 10 x 10^6/L for any baseline above 362 x 10^6/L, about 60% of patients
whose baseline exceeds 200. The simulation below therefore holds the baseline
at its typical value, 266.4 x 10^6/L, and draws between-subject variability
on `kel` and `kout` only, without comedication. Time below a level is counted
from the first to the last day spent below it, over 5 years.

```{r table3-sim}
mod_t3 <- rxode2::ini(mod, etalrbase = 0)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- bind_rows(lapply(regimens$regimen, function(reg) {
  ev <- make_events(reg, seq_len(n_sub), seq(0, 7 * 260, by = 1))
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_t3, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  s$regimen <- reg
  s
}))

time_below <- function(time, value, level) {
  below <- time[value < level]
  if (length(below) == 0) 0 else (max(below) - min(below)) / 7
}
durations <- cohort |>
  group_by(regimen, id) |>
  summarise(
    below10 = time_below(time, bcell, 10),
    below100 = time_below(time, bcell, 100),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
stopifnot(nrow(durations) == 4 * n_sub)

pi_fmt <- function(x) {
  sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", median(x), quantile(x, 0.025), quantile(x, 0.975))
}
table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,                  ~pub10_med, ~pub10,               ~pub100_med, ~pub100,
  "750 mg/m2: 2 infusions",  26.0,       "26.0 (6.4-94.0)",    42.7,        "42.7 (11.3-182.5)",
  "375 mg/m2: 4 infusions",  27.2,       "27.2 (7.6-95.2)",    44.1,        "44.1 (12.9-183.7)",
  "750 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   21.4,       "21.4 (4.3-82.5)",    38.6,        "38.6 (9.1-167.8)",
  "375 mg/m2: 1 infusion",   18.0,       "18.0 (3.7-71.6)",    35.7,        "35.7 (8.2-154.2)"
)
t3 <- durations |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    sim10_med = median(below10), sim10 = pi_fmt(below10),
    sim100_med = median(below100), sim100 = pi_fmt(below100)
  ) |>
  right_join(table3, by = "regimen") |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen)) |>
  arrange(regimen)
stopifnot(nrow(t3) == 4, !anyNA(t3$sim10_med))

t3 |>
  select(regimen, pub10, sim10, pub100, sim100) |>
  rename(
    Regimen = regimen,
    "Below 10: Pan 2019 (weeks)" = pub10, "Below 10: simulated" = sim10,
    "Below 100: Pan 2019 (weeks)" = pub100, "Below 100: simulated" = sim100
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r table3-assert}
pct <- with(t3, c(
  100 * (sim10_med - pub10_med) / pub10_med,
  100 * (sim100_med - pub100_med) / pub100_med
))
# Across rxSetSeed() values 11, 222, 3333, 44 and 2019 the median of the eight
# differences was 1.8-14.6% and the largest 11-18.8%.
stopifnot(
  # Centre: halving kel or kout moves these medians by 40% or more.
  abs(median(pct)) < 30,
  # Envelope over the eight medians of a 200-subject cohort.
  max(abs(pct)) < 45
)
round(pct, 1)
```

The simulated medians run about 5-20% longer than Table 3, the lower 2.5%
bounds agree closely, and the simulated upper bounds are longer. The ordering
of the regimens and the spacing between them, about `log(2) / kel` = 2.8
weeks per doubling of a single dose, match Table 3. The remaining gap is
in the same direction as the Figure 4 comparison (published recovery slightly
sooner) and is consistent with an unreported detail of the published
simulation (the BSA, the baseline value or distribution, or the simulation
horizon); it is not tuned away.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Parameter precision.** Values are the final estimates in the NONMEM file
  of the supplementary material, which round to Table 2. The largest rounding
  is `kout`: 0.0160 per day, printed 0.02 in Table 2. The 35-day B-cell
  half-life in the Results and Discussion is `log(2) / 0.02`; the as-fitted
  value gives `log(2) / 0.0160` = 43.3 days.
* **Residual error.** The NONMEM error model has a fixed additive variance of
  0.0001 (an additive SD of 0.01 x 10^6/L) besides the estimated proportional
  term; it is kept as `addSd = fixed(0.01)`. The zero counts were replaced by
  5 x 10^6/L before fitting (M6 method); the model does not encode a limit of
  quantification.
* **Comedication coding.** `CONMED_MTX` and `CONMED_CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE` are the
  `MTX` and `CTX` columns of the NONMEM data. The paper does not say whether
  they were time-varying or fixed per patient.
* **Body-surface area.** Not reported for the simulations; 1.33 m^2 is used
  here so that 750 mg/m^2 equals the cohort's median dose of 1000 mg. The
  per-infusion cap of 1000 mg seen in Table 1 is not applied.
* **Table 3 cohort.** Simulated with the baseline held at its typical value,
  between-subject variability on `kel` and `kout` only, and no comedication,
  for the reason given above.
* **Covariates screened but not retained** (age and sex on `kin`; azathioprine
  and mycophenolate on Emax and ED50) are listed in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Errata.** A EuropePMC search on 2026-11-25 found no correction to
  Pan 2019.
